summary: Internal SE enablement session focusing on messaging, competitive positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI/AWS, and a live demo practice. Team practiced a short 8-min demo flow, reviewed common objections around latency/cost and VPC/private deployment, and aligned on next steps for updated assets and follow-up role-play.
transcript:
Header: 2027-03-29 16:00 PT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE Manager), Jordan Lee (Clearpath CTO), Sana Ahmed (Clearpath ML Eng), Mark Rivers (Clearpath VP Product)

Topics: messaging, competitive positioning, demo flow, latency/cost objections, VPC/private deployment, next steps

[00:00] Alex Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off, todays session is a mix of messaging and demo practice, so try to be candid, call out parts that feel weak
[00:18] Priya Patel: hey team, I have a quick outline �� 1) messaging refresh, 2) quick competitive callouts, 3) live demo practice 8 minutes, 4) Q&A and next steps
[00:34] Miguel Alvarez: right, we wanna make sure our talk track maps to both hosted and dedicated/private asks since Clearpath mentioned both last week
[00:47] Jordan Lee: yeah our main concerns are latency and data residency, also curious how Redwood compares to Anthropic and Bedrock on tail latency and cost footprint
[01:05] Alex Chen: great �� we'll address that in the competitive section, and Priya will show a demo that highlights routing and fallback, so you can see graceful degradation
[01:22] Sana Ahmed: quick note, our infra team uses k8s on-prem for sensitive workloads, so any VPC/on-prem language in the demo should be concrete
[01:37] Priya Patel: noted, i'll mention Private deployment and KMS/HSM options �� also SOC2 and audit logs when relevant

--- Messaging review ---
[02:05] Miguel Alvarez: high level messaging: "Redwood is a developer-first inference platform for predictable latency and cost across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments" �� feels good but maybe too generic
[02:28] Alex Chen: we should lead with the production economics angle �� e.g., "reduce unit cost while preserving latency SLOs" �� that resonates with infra and product folks
[02:45] Mark Rivers: yeah customers don't buy models, they buy predictable bills and uptime �� call out batching, KV cache and fallback explicitly
[03:00] Priya Patel: suggestion: quick 2-line elevator: "Redwood Inference gives teams predictable, low-latency LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private environments with built-in caching, intelligent batching, and robust deployment controls."
[03:20] Jordan Lee: that reads well; maybe add a callout for observability �� token-level cost and per-route dashboards
[03:34] Miguel Alvarez: add one-liner for security: "enterprise controls: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs"

--- Competitive positioning ---
[04:10] Priya Patel: quick competitive slide �� top asks we hear: 1) "Is this just another API?" 2) "How do you compare to Anthropic/OpenAI?" 3) "Can you run in our VPC/on-prem?"
[04:28] Alex Chen: for Anthropic/OpenAI �� strength is we provide unified runtime + deployment abstraction and cost controls; public APIs may be simpler but less flexible for private deployments and predictable economics
[04:45] Sana Ahmed: specifically, Anthropic has strong model quality but we worry about vendor lock; cost and private on-prem hosting is pain with them
[04:58] Priya Patel: Bedrock is an infra play �� tight with cloud providers, but multi-tenant and less transparent performance for cross-region SLOs �� we highlight predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) as counter
[05:18] Miguel Alvarez: callout: when customers ask about latency, lead with our kernel selection and continuous batching story �� but avoid deep kernel jargon in exec conversations
[05:34] Mark Rivers: someone always asks about hallucinations and model correctness �� do we have a quick talking point?
[05:42] Alex Chen: yes, quality monitoring tied to prompt sets/evals; we can run eval suites and set regression alerts �� good to mention in demo request

--- Demo practice setup ---
[06:05] Priya Patel: OK i'm gonna run a ~8 minute demo scenario: Clearpath has a customer-facing insights chat that needs 2nd-level latency under 300ms p95, embedding search for long docs, and redaction for PHI on private data. I'll narrate and pause for objections
[06:27] (sound of a laptop, slight cough)
[06:40] [DEMO START] Priya Patel: slide 1: architecture overview �� browser -> Redwood API -> model catalog + routing -> dedicated GPU pool or private deployment. note: prefix caching and batching reduce repeated token costs
[07:02] Jordan Lee: pause �� can you show an example of fallback? like if Dedicated hits capacity what happens?
[07:15] Priya Patel: yes �� policy-based routing: we route by latency tier and cost; automatic fallback to compatible model variants or hosted capacity; plus burst options. we can show trace in console
[07:35] Priya Patel: (typing demo) invoking chat generate with function calling, streaming response appears �� p50 is ~120ms in this simulated demo
[08:02] Sana Ahmed: that simulated p50 is nice, but what about p95 under real load? we instrument with token-level traces and throughput tests
[08:22] Priya Patel: right, for p95 we recommend dedicated reserved capacity or pinned nodes; also adjust batching window to balance throughput vs tail latency
[08:41] Miguel Alvarez: small coach note �� when the customer asks about p95, show that we can run a benchmark using their sample workload in a 2-hour PoC; propose an objective metric
[08:58] Priya Patel: good call. i'll add that to the scripts

[09:15] [DEMO: Embeddings flow] Priya Patel: now embeddings �� we show indexing pipeline and caching for vector lookups plus quantization recommendations to reduce memory/cost
[09:38] Mark Rivers: question around embeddings accuracy after quantization?
[09:45] Priya Patel: tradeoffs: quantization lowers memory and cost, small hit on accuracy for dense retrieval �� we provide model-specific recommendations per workload and can run evals
[09:58] Jordan Lee: whats the typical cost delta vs OpenAI? approximate numbers ok
[10:07] Alex Chen: we usually position as "up to 60% off per-token with batching and caching relative to public API pricing for high-volume workloads" �� give a range and offer to run a cost model with their numbers

--- Role-play and objections ---
[10:35] Priya Patel: i'm going to role-play the objection "we're worried about vendor lock and long term porting"
[10:42] Priya Patel (as customer): "what if we later want to move models or run in another environment?"
[10:48] Alex Chen: (responding) "we separate control plane and runtime, let you pin model versions and export workloads �� our goal is not lock-in but predictable serving"
[10:58] Jordan Lee: that sounds okay; ask to show contract language on data portability
[11:05] Miguel Alvarez: note to Alex: have the legal snippet handy in the follow-up pack

[11:20] [DEMO: Private deployment specifics] Priya Patel: quick note on Private: can run in customer VPC or on-prem, we integrate with KMS/HSM for keys, provide audit logs and SSO/SAML for identities, and optional air-gapped package for regulated workloads
[11:45] Sana Ahmed: do we support hardware attestations? our security folks ask for that
[11:52] Priya Patel: we support KMS integration and can discuss HSM/attestation as a professional services conversation; flagging this for engineering follow-up

[12:08] Mark Rivers: silence for a sec �� how about observability �� what does the console show for debugging a slow request?
[12:18] Priya Patel: token-level traces, per-route latency heatmaps, and cost breakdown per API call; we also have tracing hooks to correlate with application logs

--- Practice feedback & coaching ---
[13:02] Miguel Alvarez: good demo overall �� timing was slightly off (8:45) but pacing is improving; two coaching items: 1) simplify the first slide, 2) when customers ask about cost, ask for monthly volume and common sequence length before giving percentages
[13:21] Alex Chen: also call out the fallback story early �� customers panic on capacity questions, so pre-empt with the routing/fallback slide
[13:33] Priya Patel: noted �� will reorder demo to show fallback earlier and add a quick benchmark ask

--- Deeper technical Q&A (customer asks) ---
[14:00] Jordan Lee: walk me through kernel selection and why that matters for long sequences
[14:10] Priya Patel: at a high level, kernel selection optimizes the compute path for sequence length distribution �� e.g., different matrix kernels for short vs long context reduce per-token latency; we test and pick by model + hardware profile
[14:27] Sana Ahmed: any specifics on GPU types you support for Dedicated? we have infer nodes with A100s and some older v100s
[14:37] Alex Chen: Dedicated supports a range; we recommend A100/Nvidia H100 for production SLOs but can support mixed fleets; we'll include recommended hardware mappings in the follow up
[14:52] Miguel Alvarez: mention quantization-friendly flows as a cost lever as well

[15:05] Mark Rivers: security question �� do audit logs include prompt text or just metadata?
[15:12] Priya Patel: configurable �� for regulated data we advise partial redaction and token-level retention policies; by default metadata + hashes but can be configured per-customer
[15:25] Jordan Lee: clouds our data residency needs by region? we may require EU-only processing for some customers
[15:32] Alex Chen: yes, regionally pinned processing and Private deployments are the path for strict residency; we'll surface compliance docs in the follow-up pack

--- Mock objection: cost vs latency ---
[16:00] Priya Patel (role-play): "Your solution is cheaper but our users will notice slower responses"
[16:08] Alex Chen: we respond with examples of dynamic batching windows and KV cache to keep p95 low while reducing token cost; show customers the trade graphs in Redwood Optimize
[16:29] Sana Ahmed: can you demonstrate the cost graph in the console?
[16:36] Priya Patel: in a live setting yes �� it shows cost per route and token breakdown, we can annotate spikes and suggest quantization

--- Wrap-up demo practice ---
[17:05] Priya Patel: wrap up �� demo flow runs through: architecture, fallback, chat demo, embeddings, private deployment, observability, next steps for PoC
[17:18] Miguel Alvarez: good. one more note: include a short script for the AE to ask the customer for concrete SLOs and monthly usage early
[17:32] Alex Chen: agreed �� we'll add an early qualification checklist to the deck

--- Q&A remainder + admin ---
[18:00] Jordan Lee: timeline question �� if we wanted a PoC, what's realistic lead time for Dedicated vs Private?
[18:12] Alex Chen: Dedicated reserved gets faster provisioning (weeks) depending on capacity and commitment; Private (VPC or on-prem) is longer (few weeks to a couple months) depending on network and security signoff
[18:30] Sana Ahmed: who is the technical owner for Private setup?
[18:35] Miguel Alvarez: SEs own the tech onboarding plus partner eng for on-prem; we'll assign a technical PM for bigger engagements
[18:48] Mark Rivers: procurement and legal process �� can you send standard contract SLAs and data terms?
[18:55] Alex Chen: yes, legal snippet + data portability example in follow up pack

--- Final recap & agreed next steps ---
[19:20] Alex Chen: recap �� we'll: 1) share updated messaging slides and demo script (Alex/Priya), 2) send competitive battlecard (Miguel), 3) customer to share sample prompts and SLOs (Jordan), 4) schedule a follow-up role-play and a PoC scoping call.
[19:42] Jordan Lee: that sounds good; we aim to have sample workload to you within 1 week
[19:51] Sana Ahmed: i'll coordinate with infra and send sequences and expected concurrency numbers

[20:10] (end of meeting audio blip, some chatter as people leave)
